Class enumeration and comparison of mixture models

Source: R/enumeration.R
enumerate_classes.Rd

Class enumeration evaluates alternative numbers of latent classes to inform model selection. enumerate_classes() fits a specified set of candidate models and summarizes their fit, classification quality, and estimation diagnostics. It supports latent profile, latent class, and latent transition models, including multilevel specifications.

For multilevel profile and class models, candidates can differ in the number of observation-level profiles or classes, the number of group-level classes, and, for continuous indicators, the within-profile covariance structure. Comparing these specifications allows the analyst to assess both the latent class structure and the assumptions used to represent variation within classes.

The function retains the fitted candidates and provides tables for comparing information criteria, posterior classification probabilities, class sizes, and convergence diagnostics. Individual models can be extracted with get_candidate() for further examination and analysis.

Usage

enumerate_classes(
  data,
  vars,
  id,
  n_profiles = 1:4,
  n_group_classes = 1:3,
  model = "basic",
  seed = NULL,
  family = "profiles",
  between_variance = c("varying", "equal"),
  time = NULL,
  ...,
  cores = 1L,
  type = NULL,
  verbose = cores > 1L
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per observation and columns containing the indicators, group identifier and, when applicable, occasion order and covariates. Use the same observations and measurement scale throughout a candidate comparison.

vars

Character vector naming the indicator columns in data. Indicator distributions are determined by type and the measurement arguments supplied through ....

id

The column identifying the groups the observations are nested in (students in schools, reports in students). Required; NULL enumerates single-level models, with a message. enumerate_lpa() and enumerate_lca() fit single-level models directly.

n_profiles

Positive integer profile counts to try. Default 1:4.

n_group_classes

Positive integer group-class counts to try. Default 1:3. With id = NULL it is 1 and may be left out.

model

The covariance structures to cross with the class counts. "basic" (the default) fits four structures: "EEI" (equal variances, no covariances), "VVI" (varying variances, no covariances), "EEE" (one covariance matrix shared by all profiles) and "VVV" (a covariance matrix for each profile). Omitting covariances between correlated indicators tends to favour additional profiles. "all" fits all 14 structures of Celeux and Govaert (1995). Otherwise, name structures by their three-letter codes, as multilpa()'s model takes them: the letters give the volume, shape and orientation of each profile's covariance matrix, each equal (E) or varying (V) across profiles, with I for no covariances. NULL crosses no structures. With one continuous indicator, codes that coincide (equal or varying variance) are fitted once; with only categorical indicators no structure is crossed. A structure set through variance_model, covariance_model, volume, shape or orientation in ... replaces the default.

seed

Optional integer random seed accepted by set.seed(). Used to reproduce the starting values for the same data and fitting controls. Invalid values raise latents_bad_argument before fitting begins.

family

"profiles" (the default) enumerates the profile model over n_profiles, n_group_classes and model. One or more of the group-class families "additive", "dispersion" and "additive_dispersion" enumerates those instead, over family, n_group_classes and between_variance; these need id, n_profiles and model are then rejected, and the result is a latents_family_enumeration, read with get_results() and get_candidate().

between_variance

For group-class families: the between-variance restrictions to cross, "varying", "equal" or both (the default). The dispersion family is always fitted with "equal". Refused for the profile family.

time

The occasion column. Enumerates latent transition models (lta()) over n_profiles (default 2:4) and n_group_classes (default 1), with every other lta() argument given in ... held fixed. model, when given, crosses those covariance structures. Only the profile family is available. The result is a latents_transition_enumeration, read with get_results() and get_candidate().

...

Additional fitting arguments passed to multilpa(), or to lta() when time is supplied. The same settings are used for each candidate. Common arguments include n_starts, max_iter, missing, categorical, centering, scaling, drop_empty and boundary. The group-class families accept only n_starts, max_iter, tol and min_variance through ....

cores

Positive integer maximum number of parallel workers; the default, 1, fits models serially. With a fixed seed, parallel and serial execution produce the same results. Parallel fitting requires additional memory. See Parallel estimation for platform requirements and the handling of interrupted workers.

type

Optional model type: "lca", "lpa" or "lta". NULL (the default) determines the model from the other arguments. "lca" treats every indicator as categorical, as multilca() does: indicators named in ordinal or count keep those distributions, and categorical adds to the set rather than replacing it. Numeric response codes are categorical with type = "lca". "lpa" requires continuous indicators and rejects non-empty categorical, ordinal or count. Both require time = NULL. "lta" requires time and takes its measurement settings from categorical, as lta() does; it does not make numeric indicators categorical. An explicit type requires family = "profiles"; leave type = NULL for group-class families.

verbose

Whether to report progress: one message each when the candidates are prepared, when their starts are fitted, and when the grid is done, with the elapsed time. The default reports when cores > 1, where a grid is usually long. Group-class families (family) are not reported.

Value

An object of class multilpa_enumeration (or the transition or family enumeration described above). Its type records the resolved model: "lca", "lpa" or "lta", or "mixed"/"family" for those grids under type = NULL. The print header reports this type. as.data.frame() gives one row per candidate, starting with its name ("profiles3_groups2"), with every criterion and diagnostic (including both entropies and, at each level, the smallest, largest and mean average posterior probability and the number of classes below a cutoff) and the candidate's warnings and error. get_results(x, "best") names the candidate at each criterion's minimum; get_results(x, "classification") gives every class's average posterior probability and relative entropy for every candidate; get_results(x, "deltas") and "knees" give model-selection evidence. summary() prints each criterion's minimum and every table, plot() draws the information criteria (and, with what, classification quality and model-selection views), get_candidate() extracts a fitted candidate, and compare_models() compares candidates selected by name.

Model selection

Information criteria summarize relative support for the candidate specifications, whereas entropy and posterior membership probabilities describe classification uncertainty within each fitted model. These measures address different aspects of the analysis. Model selection should also examine whether the selected likelihood is replicated across starts, whether estimates approach parameter bounds, and whether additional classes yield interpretable differences in response patterns. The function reports this evidence without prescribing a final number of classes.

Comparisons of class counts depend on the measurement specification. For example, additional profiles can represent residual associations that a diagonal covariance model cannot accommodate within profiles. Evaluate the number of classes alongside plausible covariance structures and indicator distributions. The candidate range and fitting controls are supplied by the analyst; the function does not expand the range automatically.

Parallel estimation

Socket workers are used on Windows and on macOS with Apple's Accelerate BLAS; these workers load the installed package, which must match the version used in the main R session. Other supported Unix configurations use forked processes. Each worker requires memory for its fitting tasks.

Depending on the model family, parallel tasks consist of individual starts or complete candidate models. The total number of workers does not exceed cores. Warnings and messages are reported in candidate order. Without a fixed seed, starting values can differ between runs.

Lost worker results are retried once with fewer workers, and a latents_worker_lost warning reports the interruption. Unrecovered tasks are recorded as failed starts or candidates; other results are retained.

Conditions

latents_bad_argument when model names an unknown structure, when it is given together with another way of setting the structure, or when it is given although no indicator is continuous; when seed is not a seed set.seed() accepts; when ... contains an argument multilpa() does not take; when n_group_classes other than 1 is given with id = NULL; when id is missing; when between_variance is given for the profile family; when n_profiles or model is given for a group-class family, or id is NULL; when time is combined with a group-class family or with between_variance; and when cores is not an integer of at least 1; and when type is invalid or conflicts with time, family or the requested measurement distributions.

References

Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (1995). Gaussian parsimonious clustering models. Pattern Recognition, 28(5), 781–793.

See also

get_candidate() to extract a fitted candidate, summary() for the criterion-by-criterion comparison.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:10, each = 10), y = rnorm(100))
candidates <- enumerate_classes(d, "y", "g", n_profiles = 1:2,
                              n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
as.data.frame(candidates)

# Numeric response codes, explicitly categorical:
codes <- data.frame(g = rep(seq_len(10), each = 10), item = rep(0:1, 50))
classes <- enumerate_classes(codes, "item", "g", type = "lca",
                             n_profiles = 1, n_group_classes = 1,
                             n_starts = 1, seed = 1)

# Single level, crossing class counts with two named structures:
single <- enumerate_lpa(iris, c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width",
                                "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width"),
                        n_profiles = 1:3, model = c("VVV", "EEE"),
                        n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
summary(single)
